proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: For the first part choose the diagram of the weighting definition, transport along the base-change compatibility lemma so it suffices to show the integral of the restricted weighting over the etale cover is locally constant, compute that integral as a fibre sum reducing to the coefficient of the target point in the pushforward of the restricted relative zero-cycle, and conclude local constancy by the smoothness lemma; for the second part define the family of zero-cycles on fibres by dividing the weighting values by the inseparable degrees, choose a sufficiently divisible integer using universal boundedness of the fibres of a quasi-compact locally quasi-finite morphism, note the construction and the base-change compatibility lemma never used the relative-cycle property so the constructed family has weighting n times w after any base change while base changes of weightings are weightings, reduce to the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring, form the relative zero-cycle beta with the same generic fibre and closed fibre equal to the specialization, observe the difference of its weighting and n times w is a weighting vanishing over the generic point, and conclude by the specialization lemma for weightings that it is identically zero, whence the constructed family equals beta; the final part follows from the same construction since inseparable degrees of finite field extensions are powers of the characteristic (source lines 1736-1798)

standard_prerequisites.use: First use: reduces part (1) to local constancy on V. Second use: its proof never used that alpha is a relative cycle, so w_alpha = n w persists after base change in part (2).

standard_prerequisites.name: Local constancy along smooth morphisms: the support behaviour of relative cycles along a smooth morphism of relative dimension (relative-cycles chapter, Lemma lemma-relative-cycle-smooth, canonical tag 0H5B)
standard_prerequisites.use: The computed fibre sum is the coefficient of v in pi_*beta, and the lemma makes that function locally constant on V.

standard_prerequisites.name: Universal boundedness of fibres: a morphism locally quasi-finite with quasi-compact source has universally bounded fibres (Morphisms chapter, Lemma morphisms-lemma-locally-quasi-finite-qc-source-universally-bounded, canonical tag 03JA)
standard_prerequisites.use: Guarantees a sufficiently divisible integer n making the constructed zero-cycles integral.

standard_prerequisites.name: Base change of a weighting is a weighting (More on Morphisms, Lemma more-morphisms-lemma-weighting-base-change, canonical tag 0F3B)
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the reduction to the discrete valuation ring case keep the identity w_alpha = n w after base change.

standard_prerequisites.name: Specialization lemma for weightings: a weighting of a locally quasi-finite morphism vanishing at all points over a point y vanishes at all points over every specialization y' of y (More on Morphisms, Lemma more-morphisms-lemma-weighting-specialization, no canonical tag in the snapshot tag table, defined at more-morphisms source line 22469)
standard_prerequisites.use: Kills the difference weighting w' = w_beta - n w, which vanishes over the generic point of the discrete valuation ring, forcing w_beta = n w and beta = alpha.

core_obligations: Prove the three-part lemma (proof lines 1736-1798). Part (1): choose the diagram with h : U to X, pi : U to V, g : V to Y as in more-morphisms-definition-weighting (tag 0F3A), set beta the restriction of the base change g^*alpha, and use lemma-weightings-pre (no tag in the snapshot table; relative-cycles line 1671) to get w_beta = w_alpha composed with h, reducing to local constancy of the integral of w_beta over pi (proof lines 1737-1748); compute the integral at v as the fibre sum of beta(u) times the inseparable times separable degrees, which equals beta(u) times the total degree, i.e. the coefficient of v in pi_*beta in z(V/V, 0), and conclude locally constant by lemma-relative-cycle-smooth (tag 0H5B) (proof lines 1749-1759). Part (2): for quasi-compact X define the family alpha of zero-cycles on fibres by alpha_s = sum over f(x) = s of n w(x) divided by the inseparable degree of kappa(x)/kappa(s), times the prime cycle [x]; universal boundedness of the fibres (morphisms-lemma-locally-quasi-finite-qc-source-universally-bounded, tag 03JA) provides a sufficiently divisible n making all coefficients integral (proof lines 1761-1774); the final statement, that n may be taken a power of the prime p when S is over F_p, follows from the same construction since inseparable degrees of finite field extensions are powers of p (proof line 1774); to see alpha is a relative zero-cycle one must check compatibility with specializations along discrete valuation rings; the construction of w_alpha and the proof of lemma-weightings-pre (second use) never used that alpha is a relative cycle, so w_alpha = n w holds and persists under base change, and base changes of weightings are weightings by more-morphisms-lemma-weighting-base-change (tag 0F3B), reducing to the case S the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring (proof lines 1775-1783); in that case form the relative zero-cycle beta with beta_eta = alpha_eta and beta_0 = the specialization of alpha_eta, so w' = w_beta - n w is a weighting vanishing over the generic point, and more-morphisms-lemma-weighting-specialization (no tag in the snapshot table; more-morphisms line 22469) forces w' = 0, whence w_beta = n w and alpha = beta (proof lines 1785-1797).
proof_roadmap: Part (1): transport to the etale localization diagram via the base-change compatibility lemma and compute the integral over pi as the coefficient of the pushforward cycle, locally constant by the smoothness lemma (proof lines 1737-1759).

Part (2) construction: define alpha by dividing weighting values by inseparable degrees and choose a sufficiently divisible n via universal boundedness; the p-power variant for S over F_p follows since inseparable degrees are p-powers (proof lines 1761-1774).

Reduction: the weighting construction and its base-change compatibility never used the relative-cycle property, and base changes of weightings are weightings, so reduce to the discrete valuation ring case (proof lines 1775-1783).
DVR case: compare with the relative cycle beta having the prescribed generic and closed fibres and kill the difference weighting by the specialization lemma (proof lines 1785-1797).
